Mapping of address to token balance, mutated by transfer and transferFrom.

SafeMath multiplication with overflow require check; declared but unused by the token contract.

Owner-only function that performs an external call to move arbitrary ERC20 tokens held by the contract.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership checks, balance mutation and allowance keys.
External call to an arbitrary spender contract via ApproveAndCallFallBack.receiveApproval after state update.
External call to an arbitrary token contract address via ERC20Interface.transfer.
Unconditional revert() in the fallback function that rejects plain ETH transfers.

edges.reason: msg.sender is assigned to the owner state variable inside the Owned constructor.
Owned constructor execution writes the owner state variable.
The _newOwner parameter is stored into newOwner by transferOwnership.
transferOwnership writes the pending owner into newOwner.
onlyOwner modifier compares msg.sender with owner before staging the new owner.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender to equal newOwner.
acceptOwnership promotes newOwner and then resets newOwner to address(0).
place constructor initializes the _totalSupply state variable.
place constructor credits the entire supply to the deployer address in balances.
totalSupply reads the _totalSupply state variable.
balanceOf reads from the balances mapping.
The to parameter is used as the credit address in transfer.
The tokens parameter is the amount moved in transfer.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender], so the caller controls the debited account.
transfer calls safeSub to debit the sender balance.
transfer calls safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.
transfer mutates the balances mapping.
The spender parameter is used as the allowance key in approve.
The tokens parameter is stored as the allowance value in approve.
approve keys the allowance by the untrusted msg.sender.
approve writes the allowed mapping.
The from parameter identifies the debited account in transferFrom.
The to parameter identifies the credited account in transferFrom.
The tokens parameter is the amount moved in transferFrom.
transferFrom subtracts the spent amount from allowed[from][msg.sender].
transferFrom mutates the balances mapping for both from and to.
transferFrom decrements the allowed mapping allowance.
transferFrom calls safeSub for balance and allowance debit.
transferFrom calls safeAdd to credit the recipient.
balanceOf uses tokenOwner as the lookup key in balances.
allowance uses tokenOwner as the outer key of the allowed mapping.
allowance uses spender as the inner key of the allowed mapping.
allowance reads the allowed mapping.
The spender parameter becomes both allowance key and external call target.
The tokens parameter is stored as allowance and forwarded to receiveApproval.
The data parameter is forwarded to the external receiveApproval call.
approveAndCall keys the allowance and call origin by the untrusted msg.sender.
approveAndCall writes the allowed mapping before the external call.
approveAndCall performs an external call into an attacker-supplied spender contract after updating allowance state.
The fallback function executes revert() to reject ETH.
The tokenAddress parameter is used as an arbitrary external contract target.
The tokens parameter is the amount transferred out of the arbitrary token contract.
transferAnyERC20Token is guarded by onlyOwner which compares msg.sender to owner.
transferAnyERC20Token calls an arbitrary user-supplied ERC20 contract via ERC20Interface.transfer.
The external call result is returned to the owner-designated address.
The a parameter feeds the addition in safeAdd.
The b parameter feeds the addition in safeAdd.
The local c holds the safeAdd result.
The a parameter feeds the subtraction in safeSub.
The b parameter feeds the subtraction in safeSub.
The local c holds the safeSub result.
The a parameter feeds the multiplication in safeMul.
The b parameter feeds the multiplication in safeMul.
The local c holds the safeMul result.
The a parameter feeds the division in safeDiv.
The b parameter feeds the division and zero check in safeDiv.
The local c holds the safeDiv result.

The _newOwner argument is only meaningful as the value written to newOwner by transferOwnership.
The to argument is only used as the credit key inside transfer.
The tokens argument is only used as the transferred amount inside transfer.
The spender argument is only used as the allowance key inside approve.
The tokens argument is only used as the allowance value inside approve.
The from argument is only used to key balance and allowance debits inside transferFrom.
The to argument is only used as the credit key inside transferFrom.
The tokens argument is only used as the moved amount inside transferFrom.
The tokenOwner argument is only a read key for balances inside balanceOf.
The tokenOwner argument is only a read key for allowed inside allowance.
The spender argument is only a read key for allowed inside allowance.
The spender argument becomes the allowance key and the external call target in approveAndCall.
The tokens argument is forwarded into the external receiveApproval call after the allowance is set.
The data argument is only meaningful as calldata forwarded to the External receiveApproval call.
The tokenAddress argument only serves as the arbitrary target of the external ERC20 transfer call.
The tokens argument is only meaningful as the amount forwarded to the external ERC20 transfer call.
